# Projects, Estimates, Invoices, and Payments

Everything in EstimateSync revolves around the project. It's the single record that ties together your customer details, estimate versions, invoices, and payment tracking — from first draft to final payment.

## Create and Find Projects

Every project starts as a draft estimate. To create one, open your dashboard and start a new project.

When you need to find existing work, use the dashboard or the active projects view. You can filter by status, browse by organization, or search by customer name. Each project card gives you a quick snapshot: the customer, project title, current status, last-updated date, and totals (once you've added estimate content). For sent or sold projects, you'll also see customer-view details right on the card.

## Understand Project Status

Your project moves through a clear set of statuses as it progresses:

- **Drafting** — You're still building the estimate. Once it's ready, you can send it to your customer.
- **Sent** — The estimate has been published and is visible to your customer. From here, you can revise it or mark it as sold.
- **Revising** — You've created a new editable version from a previously sent or sold estimate. You can send the revision or mark it sold.
- **Sold** — The work has been won. Invoice and payment tracking become available. If billing has already started, revising a sold project may follow a change-order path.

## Send Estimates and Share Links

When your draft or revision is ready, send it to publish a customer-facing estimate. If something important is missing — like a customer email or estimate cost — EstimateSync flags it and lets you review before sending.

You can edit the email introduction before sending. If you're an owner or admin, you can also save your edited introduction as the default for future estimate and invoice emails.

Need to loop someone in? When you send or resend, you can add one-time CC recipients who get a copy of that customer email. They apply to that send only — they aren't saved for next time — and they work alongside the internal copy list configured in **Account Settings**.

Each sent version gets its own shareable link. Your customer's view includes the project details, notes, room or service breakdowns, totals, any discounts, your branding, and a PDF download option. Paint items you've marked as not included stay visible in the breakdown with a **Not Included** label instead of a price.

## Confirm a Proposal

Your customer can confirm a ready estimate from its shareable estimate page by
selecting **CONFIRM PROPOSAL**. The confirmation applies to the version in that
link. When it succeeds, the project moves to **Sold** and continues into invoice
and payment tracking, while the estimate remains available for review.

## Revise, Sell, and Use Version History

Need to update a sent estimate? Use the revision workflow. EstimateSync creates a new editable version from the one you select, so your previous snapshot stays intact.

Use **Mark as Sold** when you want to mark a sent or revising estimate as won.
This moves the project into sold status and unlocks invoice language and
payment tracking. Your customer can also use **Confirm Proposal** from the
shared estimate page.

When you mark a project sold in the app, the sold confirmation offers the same
one-time CC option for the customer invoice email. Those recipients only receive
the customer email — they're never added to the team work-order email.

When a project becomes sold, the normal work-order email goes to your team,
with links to view the work order and schedule the job in a calendar. You
control who receives that email in **Account Settings**. On the work order
itself, not-included paint items appear as a *Not included* note under their room
rather than as work rows.

**Version History** lets you look back at every sent snapshot. From there, you can preview past versions, start a revision from any of them, or mark a specific version as sold.

## Track Payment Progress

Once a project is sold, payment tracking kicks in. The Payment Progress section gives you a full picture of the project's financials:

- Invoice amount and deposit status
- Paid and refunded amounts
- Outstanding balance
- Payment requests, manual payment records, and refunds

When you mark a project sold in the app, the confirmation can include a Deposit Request field while the deposit can still change. The first sale uses the organization default when configured. A later sale starts from the unpaid part of the stored deposit. You can change or clear the amount, up to the invoice balance.

The default deposit also applies when a customer uses **Confirm Proposal** or an integration marks the project sold through the inbound sales endpoint. Those sales don't show the field, so the default is requested as configured.

When a deposit remains unpaid, the customer invoice and invoice email show a **Deposit Due Now** row. That row disappears after the deposit is paid.

For the big picture, check the **Payments** card on your dashboard — it totals the open balance across your projects for the current view. Open it to see the **Open Balances** list, which starts on projects that still carry a balance and can also be filtered to show all billed projects, projects waiting on a deposit, or fully paid work. Selecting any project takes you straight to its Payment Progress.

You configure payment setup and payment links in **Account Settings**. Payment Progress on the project itself shows you what's actually happened — payments received, refunds issued, and the current balance.

## Notes and Deletion

Project notes are customer-visible — they appear on estimate and invoice output. Write them with your customer in mind.

Deleting a project is permanent. Don't delete a project unless you're sure the work should be removed entirely.
